source.title: Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Net: Selective Forgetting in Deep Networks
source.authors: Aditya Golatkar; Alessandro Achille; Stefano Soatto

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper and supplementary material; it is not garbled or cut off.
record.tranche_reason: The study uses randomly resampled labels as a baseline forgetting procedure, but does not test whether standard networks fit a completely random labeling of the full training set or generalize on true labels.
record.gate_note: The random-label baseline relabels only the cohort to be forgotten and fine-tunes on the full dataset. Its reported outcomes concern forgetting that cohort, not training error on the randomized labels or test error at chance. The cited original sources' results are not this study's own results.
record.test_reason: Random labels are used as a selective-forgetting baseline on a subset of previously learned data. The study measures forgetting against the original labels, retained accuracy, confidence and relearning; it does not measure fitting randomized targets or any other listed claim version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the authors' interpretation: Random Labels can perform well on error readouts, yet rapid relearning suggests little information is removed. Its abnormal confidence distribution may make the forgotten cohort more identifiable.
record.recipe_differences: The baseline randomly resamples labels only for the cohort to be forgotten, then fine-tunes on the full dataset; it is not the original full-training-set random-label experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset, forgetting-set size, and architecture vary across the reported random-label baseline results.

fits_no_version.finding: Random-label fine-tuning changes forgotten-cohort errors, but the authors report rapid recovery of original-label performance and abnormal confidence distributions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Random-label fine-tuning of a previously learned cohort can change output readouts without removing much information about that cohort from the weights.

record.problems: The random-label baseline is a cohort forgetting procedure rather than a full random-label training experiment. The authors' supplementary material says the information bound is computed using a single random seed; re-learn-time and entropy results are presented in figures without exact numeric values in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: The paper states that random-label baselines quickly recover performance on Df in Figure 5 and Figure 10, but the plotted values are not stated numerically. It also reports entropy behavior in Figures 4 and 9 without numerical values. These outcomes concern cohort forgetting rather than any listed claim version.

untested.parts: Fitting a completely randomized training set to near-zero error, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters.
Relative convergence time for true versus random labels and its dependence on corruption fraction.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit and steadily worsening test error across a label-corruption sweep.
Whether explicit regularizers prevent random-label fitting, and whether removing them impairs true-label generalization.
The order of learning real patterns and memorizing noisy labels during training.

record.verdict_notes: All rows concern a comparator forgetting procedure and bear on no listed version. Section 5.2 describes random resampling to produce random gradients; the supplement describes shuffling. Neither reports training error against randomized targets. Relearning and entropy findings are already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: Does not evaluate zero or near-zero training error or chance test error after randomly labeling the entire training set, or compare that setup with true labels.
Does not compare training time for fitting random versus true labels or sweep the fraction of corrupted labels.
Does not train on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Does not vary the fraction of randomly corrupted labels and measure training and test error.
Does not test whether regularization or data augmentation prevent fitting random labels or affect generalization on true labels.
Does not measure the order in which real and random labels are learned.
